thread:
alex: heads up — after yesterday's package export tweak a bunch of onboarding samples fail in edge runtimes (Cloudflare/Netlify Edge). :eyes:

maria: ahhh, which tweak exactly?

alex: we changed `exports` to force the node cjs fallback for `./node` to `./dist/node/index.cjs` and removed the automatic `./` entry. edge runtimes choke on the conditional that points at a cjs file. repro: https://github.com/redwood/sample-edge-apps/actions/runs/123456789

sam: can you paste the `package.json` snippet?

alex: sure:

```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "node": "./dist/node/index.cjs",
    "default": "./dist/edge/index.mjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```

toni: that `node` conditional is fine for node, but many edge bundlers resolve `default` differently and still try to load the `node` target because of their resolver heuristics. They end up loading a CJS file in an ESM-only runtime -> runtime error.

maria: also saw TS typing complaints in the sample apps: `types` is still pointing at `./dist/index.d.ts` but the exported members differ between the node and edge builds, so consumers get mismatched signatures.

sam: ugh. Is this what caused the auth retry tests to fail in CI? I noticed flaky `InvalidMessage` errors.

ci-bot: CI: sample-edge-apps — 2 failing jobs (auth-retry-tests). See: https://ci.redwood.ai/flow/9876

alex: yep, looks related. Edge build lazy-imports the node-only auth shim and ends up with a different runtime path.

toni: quick mitigation options:
- revert the `exports` change to keep the flat `"./"` entry so legacy resolvers see the ESM entry first
- publish a new patch with explicit conditional exports for `"import"` and `"require"` instead of `node`
- add `exports.types` mapping and ensure both entries point to the same `.d.ts` shape

maria: +1 on `import`/`require` conditional. `node` is too ambiguous across bundlers.

sam: I can put together a small repro that shows Cloudflare Workers trying to import the cjs file — will post shortly.

alex: thanks. For the short term, can we roll back the change and cut a patch? It broke new user experience during onboarding.

devops-bot: Deployment notice: rolling back `@redwood/sdk-js` to 1.7.2 -> 1.7.1 on npmjs in progress.

toni: if we roll back, also add a test that runs a minimal edge import path in CI (esbuild + Cloudflare worker runtime) so this doesn't regress.

maria: also add a TS test that compiles consumers against both builds to catch typing drift.

sam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/sdk-js/pull/2345 — includes rollback + test + note in changelog.

alex: nice. After rollover, follow-up task to publish a proper dual entrypoint layout and update the SDK doc about `exports` best practices for edge users.

toni: small checklist for follow-up:
- publish ESM `import` target `./dist/edge/index.mjs`
- publish CJS `require` target `./dist/node/index.cjs`
- `exports.types` mapping for both entries to a unified `.d.ts`
- add CI job: `yarn test:edge-resolve` (esbuild + worker runtime)
- add a short onboarding note in `GETTING_STARTED.md` about bundler quirks

maria: assigning follow-ups: sam -> repro + CI job, alex -> rollback + release, toni -> typings tests and docs.

alex: thanks all. I'll monitor the rollback. :thumbsup:

devops-bot: npm rollback completed for `@redwood/sdk-js` -> 1.7.1.

sam: posted repro: https://github.com/redwood/sample-edge-apps/issues/56 with stack trace and minimal app.

maria: great. I'll add the TS compile assertions to the tests later today.

alex: closing the loop — onboarding samples passing again after the rollback. Will re-open when we have the dual-entry patch ready. :shipit:
